Heard Sri Jai Karan Nath, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Manav Chaurasiya, learned
Aga for the State-respondent.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023.json

sentences.text:
2.  The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
84 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B, 201 IPC & 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Saifani, District Rampur, during pendency of the trial in the court below.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023.json

sentences.text: 3. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and his family members and according to the FIR, marriage of the applicant was performed with the deceased about four years before and after marriage, applicant and his family members tortured the deceased for want of jewellery and a car and on 14.7.2022, informant received an information that applicant and his family members committed the murder of her daughter i.e deceased.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is further mentioned in the FIR that when informant arrived at the village of applicant then she received information that after committing murder of her daughter, she was cremated.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023.json

sentences.text:

sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023.json

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant is husband of the deceased and on the basis of false allegation of demand of dowry, he has been made accused in the present matter and actually, deceased died due to corona and this fact was immediately informed by applicant to the informant and other family members of the deceased and after their permission, he started cremation but in the meantime, informant arrived at the time of her cremation and started making demand of Rs. Seven lacs and when applicant failed to fulfil their demand then on the basis offalse allegation, FIR of the present case was lodged.
5.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023.json

sentences.text: He further submitted that although on the complaint made by the informant, half burnt dead body of the deceased was recovered and thereafter post mortem of the dead body of the of the deceased was conducted and according to the post mortem report cause of death could not be ascertained and viscera was preserved.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023.json

sentences.text: 6. He further submitted that although he could not annex the viscera report alongwith the instant bail application but no poison was found in the viscera report.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023.json

sentences.text: He further submitted that as no poison was found, therefore, it is not a case of abnormal death and defence taken by the applicant that deceased died due to corona appears to be quite probable.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023.json

sentences.text: 7. He next submitted that applicant is having no criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 17.7.2022 i.e. for last one year, therefore, he may be released on bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023.json

sentences.text: 8. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died in her matrimonial home and there is also allegation of demand of dowry but could not dispute the fact that according to the viscera report, no poison was found.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023.json

sentences.text: 9. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023.json

sentences.text: 10. Although, applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within seven years of her marriage in her matrimonial home and there was allegation of demand of dowry and also allegation against the applicant is that he without informing the informant tried to dispose of the death body of the deceased but from the record, it reflects that at the time of cremation, informant arrived at spot and on his compliant half burnt dead body of the deceased was recovered and thereafter post mortem of the dead body was conducted and at the time of post mortem, cause of death could not be ascertained and viscera of the deceased was preserved.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023.json

sentences.text: 11. During the course of argument, learned AGA produced the viscera report and from its perusal it appears that no poison was found, therefore, the argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant that due to corona deceased died and as she died due to corona, therefore, after taking permission of the informant, he initiated the cremation proceeding but subsequently informant and his family members intercepted him and lodged the FIR of the present case, cannot be completely disbelieved, at this stage.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023.json

sentences.text: 12. Further, after viscera report of the deceased, at this stage, it cannot be said that deceased died abnormal death as per the provision of section 304 B IPC.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023.json

2 13.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023.json

sentences.text:
Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed above, in my view,
applicant who is although husband of the deceased is entitled to be released on bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023.json

sentences.text: 14. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023.json

sentences.text:
15. Let the applicant-Tinku, be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
16.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023.json

sentences.text: In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023.json

sentences.text:
17. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.

sentences.text: 5. The F.I.R. of the matter was lodged on 22.10.2022 by Amar Singh against the applicant and five other accused persons alleging therein that his daughter Veenesh was married with the applicant on 07.2.2022.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 19 September, 2023.json

sentences.text: He spent around Rs.9 lakhs in her marriage but the accused persons were not satisfied with the gifts and dowry and used to trouble his daughter for it.

sentences.text: She used to be kept hungry.

sentences.text: On 21.10.2022 he called on the mobile phone of the deceased which was not answered, then after sometimes he came to know that his daughter has been murdered.

sentences.text: 6. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.

sentences.text: It is argued that the deceased committed suicide and died which is suggestive from the post mortem report in which the doctor has found single ligature mark on her body and cause of death has been opined as asphyxia as a result of ante mortem hanging.

sentences.text: It is argued that the deceased was mentally seek person and was under treatment of psychiatrist, annexure no. 5 to the affidavit being some prescriptions have been placed before the Court to demonstrate that there was treatment going on of the deceased.

sentences.text: It is argued that trial in the matter has started and is under progress in which the witnesses of fact have been examined in which P.W.-2 to P.W.-5 have not supported the prosecution case and have been declared hostile whereas Amar Singh the first informant was examined as P.W.-1 who although in the examination-in-chief supported the prosecution case but later on has given a version of false implication of the applicant.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 19 September, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is argued that looking to the said fact the applicant deserves to be released on bail.

sentences.text: 7. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and argued that the applicant is husband of the deceased.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 19 September, 2023.json

sentences.text: Marriage of the deceased with the applicant was solemnized on 07.2.2022 and the deceased died on 21.10.2022 which is after about 8 months of marriage.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 19 September, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is argued that even the post mortem examination report shows that the deceased was having pregnancy.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 19 September, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is argued that the deceased died within seven years of marriage in her matrimonial house.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 19 September, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is argued that the trial in the matter has started and is under progress in which witnesses of fact have been examined and as such release of the applicant at this stage is not in the fitness of things.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 19 September, 2023.json

sentences.text: 8. After having heard learned counsels for the parties and perusing the records, it is evident that the applicant is husband of the deceased.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 19 September, 2023.json

sentences.text: The wife of the applicant died in her matrimonial house within seven years of marriage.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 19 September, 2023.json

sentences.text: The P.W.-1 Amar Singh the first first informant and father of the deceased while being examined in the trial, has supported the prosecution case.

sentences.text: The trial is under progress in which witnesses of fact have been examined.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 19 September, 2023.json

sentences.text: 9. Looking into the facts and circumstances of the case as well as nature and gravity of the offence no case for bail is made out.

sentences.text: 10. The bail application is, accordingly, rejected.

2. Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as Sri Arun Kumar Mishra, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
3.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 63 of 2024, U/S 498A, 302, 201, 120B IPC, Police Station Sarsawa, District Saharanpur, during the pendency of trial.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text:
PROSECUTION STORY:
4. The informant had married his daughter to the applicant as per Hindu rites on 12.3.2012 but subsequently, the applicant used to subject her to cruelty for a demand of dowry of Rs. 3 lakhs, as Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32233219/
1 such, had committed her murder sometime before 14.3.2024.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: They had even conducted her last rites and concealed the fact of her murder.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text:
ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF THE APPLICANT:
5. The applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case with a view to cause unnecessary harassment and to victimize him.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: He has nothing to do with the said offence.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: 6. The FIR is delayed and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: 7. The informant was very much present at the time of cremation of his daughter.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: She has died a natural death.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: There is nothing on record to suggest that the applicant had committed the murder.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: Although in the statement of the sons of applicant, they had stated that they had seen the husband and wife duo quarreling with each other but they had left the house for playing.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: When they returned back, they found their mother dead.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: There is no mentioning of this fact earlier on.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: 8. Two witnesses have been examined in the trial.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: P.W. 1 is the informant and P.W. 2 is the mother of the deceased person, and they have not supported the prosecution story.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: They have completely resiled from their earlier statement given to the I.O. and the allegations of the FIR.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: The witnesses have been cross-examined by the public prosecutor after declaring them hostile.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: There is no likelihood of conviction in the present case under the circumstances.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: The fundamental rights of the applicant as enshrined in Article 21 of the Constitution of India stand violated.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: 9. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: 10. There is no criminal history of the applicant.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: The applicant is languishing in jail since 17.3.2024.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text:
ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF INFORMANT/STATE:
11. The bail application has been opposed but the fact that there is no criminal history of the applicant has not been disputed.
CONCLUSION:
12. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.
13. A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt. Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32233219/
2 or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text:
The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
14.

sentences.text: Reiterating the aforesaid view the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595 has again emphasised that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that ?bail is a rule and jail is an exception?.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: 15. Learned AGA could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: 16. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned AGA.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text:
17. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences.text: The bail application is allowed.

18. Let the applicant- Tinku involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.

sentences.text: (ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

sentences.text: 19. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

sentences._hearing_file: Tinku vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024.json

2.  The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and his family members and according to the FIR, marriage of the applicant was performed with the deceased about four years before and after marriage, applicant and his family members tortured the deceased for want of jewellery and a car and on 14.7.2022, informant received an information that applicant and his family members committed the murder of her daughter i.e deceased.

10. Although, applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within seven years of her marriage in her matrimonial home and there was allegation of demand of dowry and also allegation against the applicant is that he without informing the informant tried to dispose of the death body of the deceased but from the record, it reflects that at the time of cremation, informant arrived at spot and on his compliant half burnt dead body of the deceased was recovered and thereafter post mortem of the dead body was conducted and at the time of post mortem, cause of death could not be ascertained and viscera of the deceased was preserved.
11. During the course of argument, learned AGA produced the viscera report and from its perusal it appears that no poison was found, therefore, the argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant that due to corona deceased died and as she died due to corona, therefore, after taking permission of the informant, he initiated the cremation proceeding but subsequently informant and his family members intercepted him and lodged the FIR of the present case, cannot be completely disbelieved, at this stage.
12. Further, after viscera report of the deceased, at this stage, it cannot be said that deceased died abnormal death as per the provision of section 304 B IPC.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed above, in my view,
applicant who is although husband of the deceased is entitled to be released on bail.
opennyai_summary.18_July_2023__decision:
14. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.
15. Let the applicant-Tinku, be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
16.
In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.
17. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
